List simtte's bundled example mrgsolve models

Source: R/examples.R
simtte_example_models.Rd

Returns the names of the mechanistic mrgsolve models shipped as user-facing examples/templates in inst/models/examples/. These are plain, editable .cpp model source files, not part of the package's internal Weibull/M-spline simulation engine (see sim_tte) and not used by it. They demonstrate the dxdt_p11 = -p11 * HAZ survival co-integration pattern that a user's own custom mrgsolve model is expected to follow when working with sim_tte_df directly; see "Shipped example models" below.

Usage

simtte_example_models()

Value

Character vector of example model names, suitable for passing to simtte_example_model.

Details

Discovery is a directory listing of *.cpp files in inst/models/examples/, not a maintained registry or catalog: adding a new example model in a future package version requires only adding a new .cpp file to that directory, with no change to this function.

Shipped example models

pkpd_idr_hazard

A one-compartment oral-absorption PK model coupled to an indirect-response (turnover) mediator model, in which drug exposure inhibits mediator production and the event hazard is proportional to the current mediator level. Includes between-subject variability ($OMEGA) on clearance, volume, and potency. This is the model described in the package's companion manuscript ("ODE-coupled PK/PD hazard"), shipped here as a standalone, loadable file.

pkpd_linear_hazard

A minimal one-compartment IV-bolus PK model with a hazard that decreases linearly in drug concentration from a constant baseline. No between-subject variability or turnover dynamics. Both the PK and hazard are linear, so this model has an independent closed-form survival function, making it a short, readable starting point for a custom model as well as this package's validation anchor for mechanistic hazard models (see inst/validation/ in the package's source repository – a developer-only directory, not installed with the package).

See also

simtte_example_model, to load one; sim_tte_df, the function these models are for. sim_tte_ode_models lists the built-in models for sim_tte_ode, which are a separate set.

Examples

simtte_example_models()
#> [1] "pkpd_idr_hazard"    "pkpd_linear_hazard"
